description: Chalk-cream, crazed edge to edge with fine dark fissures, and not one of them gives. In armour it refuses to come apart.
lore: Hand one to somebody new and watch the thumb. The whole surface is crazed, fine dark fissures dividing the chalk-cream into panels like a flat of dried mud, and every pair of hands new to it presses, gently, to find out how near the thing is to coming apart. It does not give. The trade keeps a short demonstration for buyers who will not take that on trust, involving a bench and the flat of a hammer, and the stone wins.

It stays cheap all the same, and the reason is honest: there is nothing to feel. In armour it pays out at the one moment you would otherwise not be getting up, and that is a hard thing to sell to anyone who has never been on the ground. [[characters/6bb1eb5a|Solveig]] keeps the fire the broken re-form beside, and has sat with what comes back — minus a little of what it was thinking — often enough to have a settled opinion. She gives every new bag-carrier heading out the same advice: past the bright stones, buy the dull one. The ones who laugh at the price have not been on the ground either. She says it pleasantly, once, and does not argue. Her fire will make the case for her some night, whichever stone they chose.
